contains.1.8.122: Design system phase 5, thirty-third part: art can share shapes (defs and use), on the same branch as 1.8.120. The art compiler writes each use out where it is placed, so packs stay plain items; with it the art format is built whole and phase 5's list is done. Nothing on screen changes.
contains.1.8.121: Design system phase 5, thirty-second part: art can loop, on the same branch as 1.8.120. A piece names parts of its drawing that move, scale and fade about a pivot through keys and close where they started; every frame is checked inside its slot, and Home, the views, the top bar and the apps picker play loops, still under reduced motion and paused on a hidden tab. No art in Budget, the Exp7 demo or the platform chrome loops yet, so nothing on screen changes.
contains.1.8.120: Design system phase 5, thirty-first part: art can repeat across its slot as whole tiles (the tile fit), on Matthew's "continue all of them" (2026-11-22). A tile piece's viewBox is one tile; the slot takes the nearest whole number of tiles each way, stretched a little so whole tiles fill it, and a piece may make at most 1024 tiles. No art in Budget, the Exp7 demo or the platform chrome tiles yet, so nothing on screen changes.
contains.1.8.119: Design system phase 5, thirtieth part: art can be filled and stroked with gradients, on Matthew's "continue all of them" (2026-11-22). The art compiler reads linear and radial gradients (pad, repeat or reflect, stops with opacity) from a piece's <defs>; a piece places them with its art and draws them as JRender paints, and text over one keeps its contrast at every stop. No art in Budget, the Exp7 demo or the platform chrome uses a gradient yet, so nothing on screen changes.
contains.1.8.118: Design system phase 5, twenty-ninth part: the motion settings nothing read are out, Matthew's "Remove those too" (2026-11-22): the easing curves, the app states and their transitions, and the motion rules. EXP7_MOTION_CONFIG keeps the version, the element poses and the state table, which the view model reads for hover lift, press scale and timings. Budget and the Exp7 demo look and move the same; saved data is unchanged.
contains.1.8.117: Design system phase 5, twenty-eighth part: the motion code that nothing reached is out, Matthew's "Unused motion code" (2026-11-22). motion-config keeps only the motion settings (EXP7_MOTION_CONFIG) that the view model reads; its JMotion state class, which took the place of JRender.ViewStates but was never made because no view record binds nodes to states, is gone with Exp7Motion, its edge table, depth layers and ambient drift. The settings only it read (parallax depth layers, integration, the tiger sweep and the empty lighting source) are gone too, on Matthew's "Remove those too". The gpu-motion script, which stepped only that class and overlay views (no view has either), is gone. JRender.ViewStates is JRender's own class again. The slabs' parity check no longer touches gpu-motion's frames. Budget and the Exp7 demo look and move the same; saved data is unchanged.
contains.1.8.116: Design system phase 5, twenty-seventh part: the motion scripts (slab-config, motion-config, gpu-motion) fill in no values and hide no faults, on Matthew's "Yes, keep going" (2026-11-22). A scroll position that is not a number leaves the slab band out; a pointer move in a window with no size moves nothing. A motion move with no edge in the state table, or into a state with no pose, does not happen and the node stays as it is; a state not in the table is not entered. Budget and the Exp7 demo look and move exactly as before.
contains.1.8.115: Design system phase 5, twenty-sixth part: the blueprint graphs (jbp) fill in no values, Matthew's "Yes, keep going" (2026-11-22). A node or edge that is not whole is left out of the graph. A value that is not a number, an input with no wire and a joy with no reader give no number, so that one item's score is NaN and ranking leaves that alternative out; division by zero still gives 0. The Exp7 demo scores and ranks exactly as before.
contains.1.8.114: Design system phase 5, twenty-fifth part: the button states script (jrviews-ux-states) fills in no values, Matthew's "Button states" (2026-11-22). It keeps only the pose that moves the TopBar's buttons and the Apps cards on hover, press, release and drag. The HTML-era layout pass wrapped around JRViews.layout (state stamps, washes, rings, inset light, glass rims, ground shadows and their node ids, the HTML pose kinds, the pressed fill and ring swaps), which nothing had reached since views became vector models in 1.8.39, is out with its exports and two hiding catch blocks. A pose is read only when it is whole (kind free, a rest that is a number, a hit box of four numbers); a node whose pose is missing a part does not move and the rest carry on. A pose takes its scale and lift as given and only moves its node. On screen nothing changes; saved data does not change.
contains.1.8.113: Design system phase 5, twenty-fourth part: the view runtime (runtime-factory) fills in no values, Matthew's "Yes, take them out" (2026-11-22). It keeps only what the views reach: the month, new, sort, filter and tocal actions, events and passes. The HTML-era page listeners (click, pointer drag, the row grip whose handler called a dragRows that no longer existed) and the actions only they reached (number pad, pickers, alternatives, row add, move and remove, jump, day clicks, ranges, joy steppers), unreached since 1.8.39, are out with their helpers. No fill-ins left (67): an action whose part is missing (a component's state, view or items list, a target's items) is left out and the atlas stays as it was; sort and filter step from the Board's start (name, all); an event carries a target only when it has one; the clock ticks only a joy with a number and a clock with its ms. Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same; saved data is unchanged.
contains.1.8.112: Design system phase 5, twenty-third part: the scoring path fills in no values and jfactor's planner is out, Matthew's "Yes, start on them" and "Take it out" (2026-11-22). jfactor keeps only its WASM/SIMD and WebGPU scorers, which JFEngine and Exp7Rank rank with; the planner (Frame, worker fan-out, Joy, JAction, JGroup, JBlueprint, JWorld, PlanIR, FastBest, field kernel), unused since 1.8.33, is out (about 4,500 lines). No fill-ins left in jfactor, jf-engine or exp7-rank (112): JFEngine.init takes no options, its probe time limits are set in one place, and a kernel row whose input is not a number scores NaN, so rank leaves that one alternative out. Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same.
contains.1.8.111: Design system phase 5, twenty-second part: the shared views code that every app's Calendar, Board and Plan run on (views-host, exp7-views, exp7-vm) hides no fault, Matthew's "Yes, take them out" (2026-11-21); he kept the evaluator's last five fallbacks ("Keep them"). The 24 catch blocks that did nothing, or stopped a motion, when a step threw are gone: closing a view, a text field's scroll watch, release and removal, blurring and focusing text fields, reading what is typed, waking the slabs, restoring a scroll, a motion's patch and draw, the reduced-motion check, the demo's live atlas and the debug hooks run as they are, so a step that throws shows. The four left record the fault: the runtime's timer, action and event steps fail alone and are recorded as CONTEXT_FAILED in views.runtime, and starting a view's runtime still fails that view in views.draw. Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same, with no failure recorded.
contains.1.8.110: Design system phase 5, twenty-first part: the atlas evaluator (eval) has no text fill-ins left (22), Matthew's "Yes, take them out" (2026-11-21). A name that is not given is not made up: an item's charge must be per, each, first or last, and an item with no charge, or another one, moves no money (it was read as each); math with no op gives no output (it was a constant); a condition with no op is false (it was >) and writes its then or else only when given (no made-up on, which is also left out of the states a view can show); a formula with no expr or out writes nothing (it was 0 into calc); a sum with no field has a count and no total (it was amount); a days node with no measure counts nothing (it was count) and with sum needs its field (it was hours); a walk must name each field it reads (they were initial, asOf, apr, payDay, cashPay, terms0); an item node with no field reads nothing (it was name). Budget saves every money item with its charge and its blueprints name what they use, so Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same and the evaluator gives the same results on Budget's atlas; only a hand-made or very old item saved with no charge stops moving money.
contains.1.8.109: Design system phase 5, twentieth part: the atlas evaluator (eval), which runs every app's calendars, ledgers and blueprints, has no || fill-ins (84). What may be missing is read through rd and ls (a frozen nothing); num gives a number or no number, never a made-up 0. A comparison with no number is false, math with an input missing gives no output, a formula whose inputs are missing writes nothing for that item and drops its earlier result (the new drop write), a walk leaves out an item missing a number it needs, a position needs its x, y and width, and an add lands on a number or starts one. A repeat of every N days without N stays on its start date (it was every day); an item with no span lasts its own day; a ledger with no opening has its flows but no balance, minimum or end; a component's max, rank, pmax or the score of an item with no scoring blueprint is left out rather than 0; a pass with no error carries no error field. A formula's via of no link still reads as 0. Text defaults such as a missing charge read as each are left for a separate decision. Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same; the evaluator gives the same results on Budget's new atlas and the test atlases, and the demo's Calendar, Board and Plan view models are the same.
contains.1.8.108: Design system phase 5, nineteenth part: the shared atlas model (atlas) has no || defaults (39). A list, map or field that is missing stays missing: it is left out of an atlas's references, its jreq and dependency walks and an alternative pick (no members means no pick, no unavailable list means none is unavailable, no needs means met, a needed key that is not text is not met). get gives only a record the atlas holds; repairing a reference sets what is given; a new joy has a value only when one is given. Nothing is named for you: an atlas needs its id and title, a new record its name and a calendar template its name (no made-up atlas, x, Calendar or Money), and each fails first without one. The money preset's starting values are named (MONEY_START) and it acts only on a calendar that has its view, states and blueprints. A new Budget atlas is the same as before, and Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same.
contains.1.8.107: Design system phase 5, eighteenth part: the shared views script (exp7-views) has no || defaults (30). rootsFor makes up no calendar, board or plan, and a view the atlas does not name is left out; making a blank atlas acts only on the parts that are there. A new Budget atlas is the same as before, and Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same.
contains.1.8.106: Design system phase 5, seventeenth part: the shared view model (exp7-vm) that lays out every app's Calendar, Board and Plan views has no || defaults (52). What may be missing is read through vmRd, vmLs and vmStr; a grid or space with no size is left out; a minimum or indent is used only when given; hover and press motion come only from the motion config; a calendar day with no risk says none. Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same.
contains.1.8.105: Design system phase 5, sixteenth part: a view draws what is saved. A view's next session keeps the state its last session gave each component, except each key the saved atlas changed since that session started, where the saved value wins (carryState). The Exp7 demo's Board now shows a saved sort or show and its buttons say it. Budget looks the same.
contains.1.8.104: Design system phase 5, fifteenth part: a Calendar, Board or Plan view writes its atlas only through a proposal. The seven direct writes made when nothing took a write (the amount's sign, a rename, prefer, unavailable, removing an alternative or a resource, and the board's sort and filter) are gone; such a write fails alone, the atlas stays as it was and the view draws it again. Removing a resource proposes dropping its item too, and sort and filter propose the board's state, adding it when there is none. ensureAlts and applyAltOps are removed; taken(ent) says whether a proposal was taken. Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same.
contains.1.8.103: Design system phase 5, fourteenth part: the shared Calendar, Board and Plan code in views-host, which every Exp7 app's views run on, has no || defaults (331). What may be missing is read through hostRd, hostLs, hostStr and hostNum. Nothing is named from an id (a board or view with no name has no title, an item with no name an empty one, a reference to a missing item is left out); the calendar's month is the one it shows (no made-up 2027-04); a step with no risk shows none; a step's effect and a category's plan line leave out what is not there; a new item, category or resource needs a name, a unit, stock or amount not given is left out, and a missing Resources list is added in the same write; a new calendar item keeps the kind its form started with. The undefined rank() call and two try blocks are gone; the starting values left are named (BOARD_START, RISK_IMPACT, VIEW_START_W). Budget and the Exp7 demo look the same; only a test board with no name loses its id as a title.
contains.1.8.102: Design system phase 5, thirteenth part: Budget's own functions in views-host have no || defaults (40). What may be missing is read through budgetRd, budgetLs and budgetStr (a frozen nothing, as in budget-flows and journal-views); the screen state is read as the Budget app started it; a charge that is not a number moves no money; every month step is given; the evaluator's charges and occurrences have no stand-in. Also fixed: Dismiss under Home's date picker closes it (the tap went to no handler, so the picker stayed open).
contains.1.8.101: Design system phase 5, twelfth part: journal-views has no || defaults (210). What may be missing is read through rd, ls and str (a frozen nothing, as in budget-flows); the screen state is read as the Budget app started it and Home opens on its home route; a deduction kind for a missing deduction, a requirement with no name, a repeat nobody picked, an alternative type the replaced item does not have and a board added with no value are left out; no made-up sort date, view size or canvas limit.
contains.1.8.100: Design system phase 5, eleventh part: Budget's part of views-host makes up no values. Day risk limits come only from meta.riskHT (Matthew, 2026-11-21: "Leave it out"): a new Budget is made with hc $500, hm $1,500, big $200 and delay 3, and a Budget without them shows no day risk and no colour legend. Boards, plan and calendar are only those meta names; an amount that is not a number moves no money and is left out of totals; budgetAmount gives no amount for an item with neither amount nor cost, and such ledger rows and balances are left out; a Budget category with no pick and no Best has no selected item; an unknown type goes on no board; an existing asset, debt or pay opens with its own kind, dates and purpose, or none. The unreached day colouring and an undefined rank() call are gone from Budget's path.
contains.1.8.99: Design system phase 5, tenth part: journal-views makes up no values. A save with no name or amount asks for it in a note under the form's title, and a debt with no term or spacing, or a pay whose deductions fail, says why. A repeat of every N days without N is left out, an item saved with no repeat shows none picked, the calendar is the one the atlas names or none, and an amount that is not a number shows nothing. The last eight try blocks and the unused payDraft are gone.
contains.1.8.98: Design system phase 5, ninth part: budget-flows has no || defaults (173 guards). What may be missing is read through four named readers, rd for a record, ls for a list, str for a field's text and opt for one thing or none. A missing record or list reads as a frozen nothing, so the part that needs it is left out and a write into it fails first instead of landing in a throwaway copy. Lists and records the script collects into are started explicitly, a copy's revision count starts at 1, and a time typed without minutes is on the hour. Layer 1 lints the whole script. Nothing changes on screen.
contains.1.8.97: The Exp7 circuit language v1, with failure built in as in Verse's <decides> (docs/circuit-language.md), Matthew's ask (2026-11-16): "The verse-like language that's part of exp7 should also feature something like Verse decides in that language so it's actually standard." Rebuilt from scratch in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly (exp7-jrender rust/lang): reading what isn't there, a false comparison, x? on false, not, dividing by zero and calling a <decides> function or a score fail instead of giving a value; a failable step may only be used inside a failure context (a rule's when and body, a score, a <decides> function, an if condition, a for filter, not, the left of or), checked when the circuit loads; what a failed context wrote is rolled back; each declaration that is wrong is left out alone and each rule fails alone, by strict fail and carry on. The host Exp7Lang (check, load, fire, score, apply) runs each rule in its own Exp7Fail context and applies a rule's ops only when it and every context around it succeed; Exp7Fail gains CIRCUIT_INVALID and CIRCUIT_FAILED. Nothing on screen changes; the demo's Circuit tab still runs the v0 parser.
contains.1.8.95: Design system phase 5, eighth part: budget-flows invents no values, by Matthew's rule (2026-11-16: a missing field stays missing and the part that needs it is left out). A missing calendar or plan id is no longer read as budget or reqs: what would be written to or read from that calendar or plan is left out and the rest of the save goes ahead. A new alternative, category or requirement copies type, flow and category only when they are there, a copied requirement keeps its date when its repeat or step is missing, and an edited pay keeps its own category. A proposal or category missing a name leaves the name out, a requirement's hint is left out without its item's name, and the plan before and after names its month every time. A charge that is not a number is left out of a month's sum, and the day risk notes are left out when a threshold is missing. Recording needs an outcome picked, a new item needs a repeat picked, and a write without its op is left out of a copy. A form's starting values are set where it opens (the Calendar's Add item at only the selected days). Nothing changes on screen while every field is there.
contains.1.8.94: Design system phase 5, seventh part: strict fail and carry on, Matthew's rule (2026-11-16), written into the spec's Rule 1: every fail point fails on its own, nothing stands in for it, and the rest carries on as if it never existed. Every part of an app now fails alone. Exp7Apps.open keeps an app closed only for a definition not in the shape of its four parts; a token set that fails its check, the pack, the blank atlas check, a route, alias, screen component or layout that is bad is recorded in its own context and left out, and Budget opens with the rest; what reads a part left out fails then, by itself (Exp7Apps.tokens, TOKEN_MISSING). Art: a bad piece is left out and the pack loads with the rest, a gap in a pack is recorded and the pack is assigned, and a slot whose art fails draws nothing while the node and the screen carry on. Budget's atlas check records each missing part and carries on, and loading saved data no longer rebuilds missing boards or moves picks saved before 1.8.57 (Matthew: "Yes, stop both"): they are left out. Nothing changes on screen while every part is there.
contains.1.8.93: Design system phase 5, sixth part: budget-rules leaves out what a record is missing. Matthew's rule (2026-11-16): a field a saved record is missing stays missing, nothing fills it in, and the part that needs it is left out with no error. A deduction with no name, kind or amount is not a line of take-home (it was named Deduction 1, counted as fixed or flagged for its amount); a schedule with no date, no repeat or missing what its repeat needs has no label (it read not scheduled, once, every day or each month), and Budget shows none; a missing number is no longer rounded to 0, a debt with no balance no longer owes 0, and pay with no gross is not given a gross of 0. A value that is there but wrong is still reported. budget-rules has no || defaults, checked by Layer 1. Also, after 1.8.92, by the same rule (a fail point fails alone and the rest carries on): each view's redraw after a save is its own fail point, so one failing no longer stops the others or Home, and the journal's model passes its options in instead of swapping the view's own, so a model that fails leaves them as they were.
contains.1.8.92: Design system phase 5, fifth part: Budget's own code stops swallowing errors, the first step in removing its fallbacks. budget-flows has no try or catch left: the plan before a recording is kept as a copy instead of text parsed back in a try, a redraw that fails after a save is no longer hidden, and a day label is no longer caught. In journal-views, the model's options, the texture limit (now always the device's own, with no guessed 8192), the screen density, preparing a plan switch and the plan-step scroll no longer hide a fault; a switch whose save throws tells the person it was not saved and still fails. Nothing changes on screen. The try sites left in journal-views (8) and the literal defaults in Budget's scripts guard the shape of saved records, and go once Matthew decides how a record missing a field is handled.
contains.1.8.91: Design system phase 5, fourth part: pressed in the Calendar, Board and Plan views. Every view component declares pressed and both view packs (exp7-views and budget-journal's view pieces) draw it, as hover where a piece draws a hover and as idle otherwise. JRViews draws a view node pressed while it is held, hover under the pointer and its rest otherwise, from its looks (setDown, artState, itemsOf), as Home does; the views' hovers and the chrome keep only n.looks (and the chrome's n.pose), and the runtime's state layer only moves a design node. Nothing changes at rest; a press on a view node shows its hover drawing. Removed: JRViews' hovItems, Exp7Art.hover, the chrome's base, hov, press, uxBorderAt and baseBorder.
contains.1.8.90: Design system phase 5, third part: every art state is drawn live. Exp7Art.draw draws a node's rest state (n.rest: selected for a picked day, choice, toggle, hour, quarter or hour row; disabled for an Accept band that can't be pressed; idle otherwise), and a rest the component does not declare fails with COMPONENT_INVALID. Exp7Art.look and looks give a node's items in each live state (hover, pressed, focus) that draws differently from its rest, kept on the node as n.looks by place and the views' hovers. Home draws a node pressed while it is held, hover under the pointer, focus while it has keyboard focus and its rest otherwise, redrawing only that node. With Budget's pack as written pressed draws as hover, so a press shows the hover drawing; nothing changes at rest. Removed: Home's hover-only swap (hovItems). Budget's views still swap hover only.
contains.1.8.89: Design system phase 5, second part: the field being typed in is drawn on the canvas from Budget's tokens and art. A tapped text field lays a LiveField (the new component, its box art in Budget's pack) over its target and puts a JRender TextField on it, styled by Exp7Components.liveStyle from Budget's tokens (body type, ink, caption ink for a placeholder, fieldPad, and the new colour token selection). screenLayout takes live, the open field's act, and fails with DATA_MISSING when it is left out or the screen lacks that field. Home keeps the open field as state, carried by its rollback; Enter keeps what was typed, Escape drops it, a tap elsewhere keeps it. A deduction's name opens with its name. Removed: the page input and its styles, overlayRect, overlayCorrection, placeFieldEl and window.__budgetFieldOverlay.
contains.1.8.88: Design system phase 5 starts with Budget: an Exp7 app is one definition, its atlas, token sets, art pack and screens, declared with Exp7Apps.define and checked whole by Exp7Apps.open when the page loads. A part missing or unknown, a token set that fails its check, a pack that does not load or cover the components, a screen component not registered or not in the pack, a route named twice, an alias that leads nowhere or a blank atlas that fails the app's own check fails with APP_INVALID (or the part's own code) and nothing opens; every Budget layout reads its tokens and routes from the opened app. Budget's atlas make, load and check move out of its package into the definition; the package loses its own board types, theme defaults, default view styling, migration and healing copies, its try/catches and the .jrerr error box. A failed draw keeps the last screen and tells the shell; a failed boot tells the shell once. Saved atlases lose a stale view theme on load. Nothing changes on screen.
contains.1.8.87: One font for measuring and drawing: every text item names the font it was measured in and JRViews draws it in that font. View, journal and chrome tokens name their fonts (font, fontStrong): the platform look DejaVu Sans, Budget Source Sans 3. A token set naming a font that is not embedded fails with FONT_MISSING; a character a font lacks fails with GLYPH_MISSING. The views' marks (arrows, ticks, triangles, stars, dots) are the new Mark component's art in both packs, each in the tone of its text, holding a blank U+FFFC place. A bold label wider than its room shrinks to fit on one line. DejaVu Sans gains Latin Extended-A. Removed: the core's font try/catches, window.__jrJournalFonts, the drawing code's default fonts, JRViews.font() and fontBold(), the demo's own glyph walk. Budget's journal screens unchanged.
contains.1.8.86: Design system phase 4, part 4c: the Exp7 demo's Paths, Calendar, Board and Plan tabs on canvas, so every demo tab is an Exp7VM model drawn by Exp7DemoUI. Paths shows the whole flattened atlas as a tree of node rows (open or close on a tap, expand all, collapse all) or a flat list, with a prefix field, a search, copy and the last proposal's tones. The Calendar, Board and Plan tabs draw their JRViews view above a screen with the view's status, the proposals as buttons with the result as a note, the side panel (discrepancies, ranking and history, steps, what-if, dependencies) and the deep paths. Path rows (Paths, the Atlas inspector, the deep paths) are path, value and copy, with type and owner on a line under. Exp7VM: a squeezed table keeps its buttons whole. The proposals' labels and the views' notes have no arrow or minus sign. Removed: the views host's jvStatus, discHTML, planSide and vbtns, renderPaths, refreshPaths, the four HTML sections, their handlers and styles. Budget unchanged.
contains.1.8.85: Design system phase 4, part 4b: the Exp7 demo's Two writers, Storage and Circuit on canvas. Two writers (the collaboration card, the network and sync controls, Alice's and Bob's edits and entries, the merge order, the diff, the path inspector and Show or Hide for each replica's Plan and Board views), Storage (the batch log, the 5000-op test and the per-path statistics) and Circuit (the rule source parsed as you type, the rules, the event arguments, what fired, the canonical print and the scores) are Exp7VM models drawn by Exp7DemoUI. Checkboxes are toggle buttons, menus are chips, folding sections are Show and Hide buttons, and tables merge columns to fit a phone. The collaboration engine's refusals are recorded in Exp7Fail. A multiline field grows to the lines its text wraps to, and another tab opens at its top. Removed: the lean's Doc and Panel helper script (Exp7Experiments), the collaboration DOM script, renderSync, renderLog, renderScores, renderSyncDiff, renderPathStats, renderInspector, the three DOM sections and their styles. Budget unchanged.
contains.1.8.84: Design system phase 4, part 4a: the Exp7 demo on canvas. Its frame (title, codec chip, Copy diagnostics, the ten tabs and the diagnostics box), the Atlas, the Proposal console, About and the path inspectors are Exp7VM models drawn by JRViews with the platform's view tokens and the exp7-views art, through a new Exp7DemoUI in the demo; a tap runs the control's act through its screen's handler, and text fields are JRender TextFields. Exp7VM can now draw text runs, code text, multiline and filling fields, notes in ok, bad and warn tones, warn chips, button cells and toned rows in tables, and tappable panels; the views use none of it, so Budget and the views draw the same. New tokens: warn and the note and row tones; new art variants in exp7-views and budget-journal. A screen with a character the fonts lack fails with GLYPH_MISSING instead of drawing a box. A screen that can't be laid out keeps its last frame and records the failure; the demo reports ready only once its screens have drawn. Removed: the demo's Budget mode (unreached since Budget has its own slot: its atlas, IndexedDB store, modes, type bar, rank panel, examples and window.exp7 entries), the codec's optional path and estimates, bootStep and the try and catch around renders and diagnostics, the clipboard's execCommand fallback, renderBatch, renderAtlas, and the HTML header and tab bar. Listed changes: everything that moved is drawn on canvas (body font for code, steppers for sliders, YYYY-MM-DD fields for dates, chips for the op menu, one column, 620 px inner scroll, tabs no longer sticky, Prefer and Unavailable buttons for the star and no-entry symbols, and words for other characters the drawing fonts lack, Best and unavailable chips, diagnostics in a canvas note). Two writers, Storage and Circuit are part 4b; Paths and the views' side panels part 4c. Tests in exp7-jrender tests/layer4-demo.mjs.
contains.1.8.83: Design system phase 4, part 3: the journal's plan, monthly expenses and cash views on components, tokens and art. A journal node in a view model is laid out by Exp7Journal.viewLayout from new components (ViewHead, DateBand, Label, MoneyRow, TotalRow) plus Note and Row, in the views.journal:budget failure context; its rules, month band and Home's keyboard focus ring (FocusFrame) are five more budget-journal pieces drawn in SVG with the studies, and its sizes are 26 more Budget tokens. Home draws the focus ring before anything is shown and keeps the last frame (and the old focus) when it can't. A journal kind with no layout (calendar, agenda: not reached from the app) and a cash row with no amount now fail. Removed: journal-views' colour, type and spacing tables, hand-drawn chevrons and marks, the old hand-placed layout, Exp7Journal.type, space, colors and glyphs, and Home's plan picker and date menus, which nothing could open. Same as 1.8.82 to 1/64 px, which moves glyph-edge antialiasing only (0 px in Chrome with 1.8.82 rounded the same way), except: names and notes that were cut off at the edge now wrap, the ledger's covered heading text is gone, and a view's navigation tap area is the view's height. Tests in exp7-jrender tests/layer4-journal.mjs.
contains.1.8.82: Design system phase 4, part 2: the platform's top bar and Apps picker on components, tokens and art. New shared script design-chrome registers TopBar, ChromeButton, Avatar, AppsPanel and AppCard, and Exp7Chrome.layout lays out a bar or a picker from a model in its own failure context. Every face, bevel, ring and shadow comes from a new art pack, exp7-chrome (6 pieces, drawn in SVG with the studies), and the sizes from a chrome token set (Exp7Tokens.chrome). PlatformChromeJR builds models instead of HTML; its local paint, default apps list, default avatar box, width stand-ins, photo fallbacks and try and catch blocks are gone. A bar or picker that can't be laid out keeps its last frame and records the failure. Nothing changes on screen, except that a selected app card goes back to its own gold when the pointer leaves it. The picker now redraws when the window is resized.
contains.1.8.81: Design system phase 4, part 1: the Calendar, Board and Plan views on components, tokens and art. New shared script design-views registers the view components (Panel, Button, Chip, InputBox, DayCell, DayStep, TableRow, and for Budget DateChevron and FocusRing). The views draw every face, shadow, tint, outline and rule from art: a new exp7-views pack for the platform look and twelve view pieces added to budget-journal for Budget's. Views take a view token set; the stock and journal skins, the default view tokens, the field style default and the views' error page are gone, and a view that can't be laid out keeps its last frame. The renderer is the JRender build from exp7-jrender #8 (GPU group transforms, wrap baselines), unused so far. Nothing changes on screen: the views lay out byte for byte as in 1.8.80. TopBar and the Apps picker are part 2.
contains.1.8.80: Design system phase 3: art slots live. New shared script design-art: an app's look is its art pack, checked when it loads (every slot of every component, in every variant and state, inside its box, text over it readable), and art can be swapped for the app, one screen or one item; a swap that fails keeps the art there was. Budget's first pack (budget-journal, 43 pieces) draws today's look: it is drawn in SVG with the studies, compiled in exp7-jrender and embedded here. Every Budget component now places art in its slots instead of drawing in code (chevrons, rules, day cells and their tints, marks, field boxes, radio, check box and star, toggles, the mint band, time cells, the selected hour), and hover comes from each piece's own hover drawing. The glyph and mark drawing code and 19 tokens only it used are gone. Nothing changes on screen: the draw lists are byte for byte those of 1.8.79.
contains.1.8.79: Design system phase 2. Every Budget screen besides Home is now laid out from design components inside a failure context: the day schedule, a day item, add an item, the pay, debt, activity and cash forms (with the Field, Choice, Every, Toggle, Pair, PrimaryBand, TimePicker, FieldDatePicker and BackBar components), edit and record, alternatives, the category, requirements, the switch review (BeforeAfter), monthly expenses, and cash and owned items. Every action runs in a failure context: if the screen it leads to cannot be laid out, nothing changes and the last screen stays. The fixed-coordinate painter (paintScreen and flowShift), the per-screen layout code and the static study screens are gone; a route with no screen fails with DATA_MISSING instead of showing a sample. Alternatives opened from a day item with none yet now show that item instead of the first plan step.
contains.1.8.78: A fuller journal font. Source Sans 3 Regular and Semibold now have every Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A letter, plus what the font has of Latin Extended-B, Latin Extended Additional, punctuation and currency signs: 687 characters each, was 120. A name such as "Café" or "Łódź" now draws on Budget Home; before, it stopped Home with GLYPH_MISSING. The 120 old glyphs are kept byte for byte and the font metrics are unchanged, so text without accents lays out exactly as in 1.8.77. The font licence (SIL Open Font License 1.1) is embedded with the fonts. Greek, Cyrillic, separate combining accents and emoji are still not in the font.
contains.1.8.77: Design system phase 1. New shared scripts: design-fail (failable steps and failure contexts that roll back), design-tokens (Budget's complete token set, checked as a whole), design-bounds (bounds, the readable rect table, text measured and shrunk to fit by JRender only) and design-components. Budget Home is laid out by components inside a failure context, with the same layout as 1.8.76: a few headings and labels sit 0.4 to 2.3 px higher because text is now placed from the font's own metrics, and a long entry name wraps instead of ending in an ellipsis. The text width estimate and the substitute journal font are gone.
contains.1.8.76: Budget data has a Clear data button for a fresh start (account menu, Budget data). It asks first and names what goes: the budget on this device and, with GitHub connected, the sealed copy in the data repo. Other Exp7 apps are not touched, and this device keeps its sync key. The repo copy is deleted first; if that fails nothing is cleared. The Budget data box now shows when signed out too, where Clear data clears this device only.
contains.1.8.75: Fix: Accept on the plan switch review now switches the plan. Before, it only started a proposal and still said "Plan updated". The requirement answers are saved with the switch: Reuse a copy makes a separate copy for the new choice, starting when it does; Not needed and Needs its own are recorded; requirements added for the new choice are added. The plan changes only when the save is accepted, and says so; otherwise the current plan stays. Answers belong to one step and one choice, so the next alternative's review starts unanswered. The requirement status (Not decided, Needs its own...) now shows on the right instead of off screen, and the review says "Carried over from the choice in use." After a switch, the next alternative is reviewed against the requirements of the choice now in use: a Reuse copy in place of the original, Not needed left out, Needs its own kept, and those made for that choice added. A copy of a copy keeps the original name.
contains.1.8.74: Budget on a phone (section 1). The journal fills a 390 pt phone screen with no side margin; the Home mini month has a plain-words legend and the selected day's reason wraps; the month picker opens inline under the heading with drawn arrows and pushes the rows down, and the full-page month view is gone. The schedule page has a Home back row, an Add row and an All day section. Fields keep what was typed when you tap the next field, and the time grid opens on the same tap. Forms show empty values instead of blanks, and labels move with notes that wrap. Adding an alternative names the real item, the star decides preferred, the new alternative is charged like the item it replaces, and a new requirement starts empty. The switch review shows the person's own plan with Before and After stacked. Debt calculated rows are no longer tap targets. A long step or requirement name wraps and pushes the choices under it down instead of overlapping them.
contains.1.8.73: Fix: Home scrolls again after opening a plan step and going back. Returning to the plan step was re-applied on every scroll, so Home snapped back to it; it now runs once and ends at the first wheel, touch, pointer or key input, or after a moment.
contains.1.8.72: Fix: Budget Home no longer stops with "seeded.map is not a function" when opening Requirements for a new alternative. An item's jreq is a single reference, not a list; the requirement list is now seeded from a reference, a list, a group or a record, and a reference shows the named item.
contains.1.8.71: Calendar-first and data-repo fixes. The data repo is created private by itself once GitHub access works (no create button, never from a half-typed repo name, never overwritten) and every failure says what GitHub reports while local saving continues. Items with no date open their edit page with the date picker so they can be dated, and join the calendar once dated; Change applies to this occurrence or this and future without rewriting earlier ones; Record what happened is saved to the occurrence (this occurrence only unless chosen otherwise, with the item and its planned amount shown); a day row shows that day's recorded or changed amount; Specific dates each month repeats on those days, and the days box shows what will be saved (the date's day until changed); day rows say how an item repeats in words; a tap on Save or a row while a field is still open now lands on the first tap; tapping a calendar entry opens that item's own page (name, day, time, repeat, amount) instead of the sample item; the date and tab refresh keeps the tapped entry and a form's draft; real schedules no longer say their values are sample data; an amount entered on the calendar is the cost each time (not split across the month's dates); pay on the calendar is the take-home. Old Board asset, debt and pay entries open the selected calendar day; Budget has no what-if path; cash is never inferred from a name.
contains.1.8.70: Home has one way to open a day's schedule (second tap on the selected mini-month day). Activity date pickers expand inline; Repeat subrows reflow; times are 24-hour; Amount has one label. Plan lives only on Home, with wrapped step text and a back stack to the step. New alternatives and new requirements share date/time/repeat fields.
contains.1.8.69: Day and Plan entry; form overlays sit on the drawn box, including a Safari width correction; date, time, and debt as-of are real pickers; Repeat, deductions, and debt fields persist onto the agenda calendar; all-day pay, debt, and cash rows appear on the day schedule; Save debt opens the as-of day.
contains.app: 1.8.68: Budget journal back controls use a drawn chevron plus Home/Plan text (the platform bar no longer uses a Unicode arrow that became tofu); long row names and selected items never overlap (two-line or ellipsis); Add to <day> is visible on the selected calendar day and opens the four-kind chooser; a Plan row opens the alternatives list with + Add an alternative, then category, preferred star, requirements review, and Plan switch Before/After Accept; monthly expenses lists Income/Expenses dated through today and Scheduled this month without a 40-row cap, with the month total after the last row and a scrollable sticky-canvas page; Cash and owned item rows open the as-of calendar day and no longer share a full-page Home hit; CSS pt equals design pt (host size from CSS, not device pixels).
contains.chromeJr: PlatformChromeJR: bar and Apps picker as Exp7Chrome models (design-chrome components, exp7-chrome art, chrome tokens; 1.8.82); JRDI circular avatar photo, initials when there is no photo or it cannot load; Budget tabs in hostDoc
